headline: Revenue grows, but a settlement charge cuts profit
summary_short: Bank of America reported Q3 2026 revenue of $30.0B (+3% y/y) and EPS of $0.91, down from $1.04 on a $1.2B regulatory settlement charge ($1.08 adjusted).
summary_long: Revenue rose 3% y/y to $30.0B as net interest income grew 8% to $16.4B and asset management fees rose, offsetting lower sales and trading revenue and investment banking fees. A $1.2B regulatory settlement charge ($0.17 per share) lifted noninterest expense to $19.7B and cut net income to $6.9B; adjusted net income was $8.1B. Provision for credit losses was $1.3B and net charge-offs fell to 0.44% of loans. Average loans grew 6% and average deposits 2%. CET1 was 10.9% and the bank returned $8.3B to shareholders, including $6.0B of buybacks.
confidence_notes: Net income and EPS are GAAP and include a $1.2B non-tax-deductible regulatory settlement charge; adjusted figures ($8.1B, $1.08) are non-GAAP as defined by the company. The y/y delta for net income uses the release's rounded $B figures ($6.9B vs $8.3B). The q/q EPS delta compares $0.91 with the shard's prior-quarter value of $1.22. Revenue is net of interest expense. The release states no guidance, so no guidance entries were written.

drivers.explanation: The CEO cites organic growth, deeper client relationships and growth in client deposits, wealth flows and consumer activity, while noting lower investment banking and sales and trading revenue.
Higher net interest income and asset management fees were partly offset by lower sales and trading revenue and lower investment banking fees.
Driven mainly by higher loan and deposit balances, higher Global Markets-related NII and fixed-rate asset repricing; net interest yield rose 15 bps to 2.16%.
Noninterest expense rose $2.4B including a $1.2B regulatory settlement charge; excluding it, net income was $8.1B against $8.3B a year ago.
Provision was relatively flat y/y as net charge-offs eased; the release reports a net reserve release of $80 million.
